title: May Required on name update, when update is served by PUT, which ignores the key?
description: ST-DECL-INV25 and ST-DECL-UC07-R01 say Required on MAY name update. ST-DECL-INV25, ST-DECL-UC07-R02 and the field Required on (ST-DECL-EN13) say only operations served by POST or PATCH may be named, because PUT ignores the key. ST-DECL-SP08 is satisfied by any operation that GET, PUT or DELETE serves. The generated routes serve update by PUT and patch by PATCH (internal/generator/restapi/http_routes.go). Reading (a): update in Required on means the patch operation, or update is served by PATCH, and checking accepts it. Reading (b): update is served by PUT, so checking refuses update in Required on, and the MAY clause is removed. Reading (c): the key applies to PUT update too, and the clause on PUT is changed. The tests leave update and custom operations out until this is decided. Recommendation: (b), as SP08 and the routes already say.

title: What in a declaration states the entries of a transfer, so that checking can refuse a transfer with one entry?
description: ST-DECL-INV27, ST-DECL-SP13 and ST-DECL-UC08-R06 say checking MUST refuse a transfer with one entry, and SP13 says a transfer code or a transfer example states the entries. The ledger settings (ST-DECL-EN14) give transfer codes only as names, and no record defines a transfer example or the entries of a code. Reading (a): a transfer code declares its debit and credit accounts, and checking refuses a code with one; the model then needs those fields. Reading (b): the rule is behaviour of the generated service, which refuses a transfer request with one entry or entries that do not balance, and checking has no part in it. No test is written for SP13 or UC08-R06, and the invariant test of INV27 leaves this clause out, until this is decided. Recommendation: (b) for the runtime rule, with (a) only if transfer codes are to name accounts.

title: How does a declaration name the system principal, and what does checking read to hold that it is a service-account subject?
description: ST-DECL-INV24 and ST-DECL-UC06-R03 say a system principal MUST be a service-account subject the schema grants relations to. A binding says runs as system (ST-DECL-EN05), and Subject from identity (ST-DECL-EN11) says a system principal is a service-account subject, but no field names the principal or its subject type. Reading (a): checking refuses a declaration with a binding that runs as system when the schema grants no relation to a service-account subject type; the declaration then needs to name that type. Reading (b): it is behaviour of the generated service, which asks the provider for each decision of a system binding as a service-account subject and never skips the decision. The tests cover the bypass flag of INV24 and UC06-R03 and leave the system principal out until this is decided. Recommendation: (a), with the subject type named in the authorization setting.

title: Does an experimental acceptance still hold on its own date, and in which time zone is the date read?
description: ST-DECL-INV16 says a declaration MUST NOT be accepted after the date of an acceptance it holds, and ST-DECL-UC03-R04 says checking fails when an acceptance is past its date. The field Accepted until (ST-DECL-EN07) is a date with no time. Reading (a): the acceptance holds to the end of its date in UTC, and checking refuses from the next day in UTC. Reading (b): the acceptance holds to the end of its date in the local time zone of the machine that checks, so two machines can disagree on one day. The tests check the day before and the day after the date and leave the date itself out until this is decided. Recommendation: (a), so that every check agrees.

title: Which fleet query shows the reason for a default left, and the public operations with their reasons?
description: ST-DECL-UC05-R02 says the fleet MUST show both reasons for tenancy kind single and audit off, and ST-DECL-UC06-R07 says the fleet shows each public operation with its reason. The terms Reason (ST-DECL-TM23) and Public operation (ST-DECL-TM24) say the same. No query or read model of the fleet (ST-DIS-RM01, ST-DIS-QRY05, ST-DIS-CLI06, ST-DIS-CLI08) holds these reasons, so a test cannot name what to read. Reading (a): stego fleet measures (ST-DIS-CLI08) gives, for each service, each default it left and each public operation, with the reason, from the committed record; the record and the read model then need those fields. Reading (b): a new fleet query lists them. The tests cover the checking clauses of UC05-R02 and UC06-R07 and leave the fleet clause out until this is decided. Recommendation: (a), so the sweep that already reads the records shows them.

title: Does plan or apply refuse an existing pin to a withdrawn digest before the withdrawal's fail date?
description: ST-GEN-INV15, ST-GEN-UC03-R04, ST-GEN-UC04-R04 and ST-GEN-PO02 say that plan and apply refuse a pin that is withdrawn, with no date condition, and ST-DIS-SP04 makes a digest withdrawn whatever the date. ST-DIS-UC07-R02 and step ST-DIS-UC07-FL-S03 say that a withdrawal carries the date after which the digest fails, and that validate fails after that date; ST-DIS-UC07-R03 refuses only a new pin at once. Reading (a): plan and apply refuse every pin to a withdrawn digest at once, and the fail date only tells validate when to fail. Reading (b): plan and apply refuse a new pin at once, and an existing pin only after the fail date, as for a supersession. Recommendation: (b), because a fail date and the word new in ST-DIS-UC07-R03 have no use under (a). The tests written on 2026-11-04 cover only the cases on which both readings agree: a withdrawn pin past its date, and a new pin to a withdrawn digest.

title: What VEX statement does the sweep emit for a checkout with no readable record?
description: ST-DIS-UC02-R04 asks for one OpenVEX statement per service and advisory with the status affected, fixed or not_affected. ST-DIS-UC02-R02 says that a checkout with generated output and no record is reported as unknown and never left out. For such a checkout the sweep cannot know the status. Option (a): emit a statement with the OpenVEX status under_investigation, which adds a fourth status to ST-DIS-UC02-R04. Option (b): emit no statement for it, and name it as unknown in the sweep's output beside the VEX document. Option (c): emit affected, so that no unknown service passes as safe. Recommendation: (a), because it keeps the service in the document and says what is known; it needs a change to the statement of ST-DIS-UC02-R04. The tests written on 2026-11-04 count statements only for checkouts with a readable record.

title: How is a clause that the platform carries out proved?
description: ST-DLV-UC05-R05 says that the platform's GitOps flow MUST run the environment check and that Argo CD MUST NOT apply an overlay whose check fails. ST-DLV-UC03-R06 and ST-DLV-PO03 say that the platform's gate MUST enforce the delivery policy that the pipeline carries. STEGO writes the check and the policy file, but the GitOps flow, Argo CD's sync and the gate are the platform's. Reading a: STEGO proves these clauses with a test of its own, against a reference platform that STEGO keeps as a fixture (a GitOps repository whose CI runs stego env check as a required check before Argo CD reads the branch, and a gate that evaluates the carried policy file), and STEGO also supplies that CI step or gate setting. Reading b: the clauses are the platform's obligations, which STEGO does not prove; STEGO proves only that the check fails and that the policy file is the one the check evaluates, and the records say that the platform provides the rest. Recommendation: reading b, with the platform's part recorded as provided by the platform, since ST-DLV-UC01 says the platform owns everything that comes from the environment, and a fixture of STEGO's own proves only the fixture. No test is written for ST-DLV-UC05-R05 or for the gate clauses until this is decided.

title: Does a verified compiler release move the pipeline pin directly, or only through a new ci-pipeline version?
description: ST-DLV-PO02 says that, when a published compiler release is verified, Write the delivery pipeline MUST read the verification record of the release and move the service's pipeline pin to that release. ST-DLV-INV04 and ST-DLV-UC04-R01 say that every pinned reference MUST come from the registry's ci-pipeline component. The two differ when the verified release is newer than the release the ci-pipeline component pins. Reading a: the policy reads the verification record and writes its pin into the CI file, and the ci-pipeline component does not pin the STEGO checks. Reading b: the policy moves the pin only when a platform engineer releases a ci-pipeline version that names the verified release, as the main path of ST-DLV-UC04 says; the verification record only lets that version be released. Recommendation: reading b, because it keeps one source for every pin, which ST-DLV-INV04 exists for, and the policy text then says that it waits for the new ci-pipeline version. No test is written for ST-DLV-PO02 until this is decided.

title: Does the import rule of a fill hold for its test files too?
description: ST-EXT-INV05 says that a fill's code MUST import only its slot's contract package, the Go standard library and the fill modules that the declaration lists. ST-EXT-UC01-R03 says that STEGO records no evidence for a fill that imports anything else. ST-EXT-UC04-R01 names a fill's code and its tests as two different things. Reading a: the rule holds for each Go file in the fill folder, test files too, so a test cannot import a test library such as testify unless the declaration lists it. Reading b: the rule holds for the files that are built into the service, and a test file can import any module that the project's go.mod holds. The test plan has no test of the imports of a test file until this is decided.

title: What is the contract package of one slot, when the generator writes every slot's contract into the one package out/slots?
description: ST-EXT-INV05 and ST-EXT-UC01-R03 let a fill import only its own slot's contract package. The generator writes the contracts of all slots into one Go package, out/slots, so a fill for before_create that imports out/slots can also use the types of before_delete. Reading a: out/slots is the contract package of each slot, and the import rule does not separate one slot from another. Reading b: the contract of each slot MUST be a package of its own, so that the import check can refuse the contract of another slot; this changes the generated layout. Reading c: the check reads the identifiers that a fill uses, not only its imports. The test plan tests imports outside out/slots only, until this is decided.

title: When two components of the active set declare a slot of one name, which fills does the list of fills for that name show?
description: stego registry fills takes --slot alone (ST-SUP-CLI06), and ST-EXT-UC03-R02 refuses a slot name that no component of the active set declares. stego fill create takes --component for a slot name that more than one component declares (ST-EXT-CLI01), so two components can declare one slot name. The fill catalog (ST-EXT-RM01) has no component field. Reading a: the list shows the fills of the slot of each such component, and each line names the component. Reading b: the list refuses the name as ambiguous, names the components that declare it, and takes --component as fill create does. The test plan has no test with two components that declare one slot name until this is decided.

title: Does a change to a .proto file that a slot contract imports make the slot's fills stale?
description: ST-EXT-DS01 computes the digest of a slot contract from the slot's .proto file alone. A slot's .proto file imports other files: before_create.proto of rest-api imports stego/common/types.proto, which defines CreateRequest and Identity. ST-EXT-UC04-R01 makes a fill stale when its slot contract changes. Reading a: the contract is the .proto file alone, so a change to types.proto leaves each fill qualified, although the messages that the fill reads change. Reading b: the contract digest MUST also cover each file that the slot's .proto file imports; this changes ST-EXT-DS01. The test plan tests ST-EXT-DS01 only with changes to files that the contract does not import, until this is decided.

title: Against what does STEGO check the compiler build that a record names, now that the record is the state file?
description: ST-GEN-UC02-R02 says that when the record names a compiler or registry digest that the service's own state does not hold, STEGO reports the record as broken. Since the decision of 2026-10-27 the record is the state file, so the only other state in that file is the input manifest. ST-GEN-INV02 makes the input manifest name the same declaration digest and registry reference as the record, and the input manifest holds no compiler build and no registry content digest. Thus the registry clause has a test (a registry reference that differs from the input manifest's), and the compiler clause has nothing to compare with. Option (a): the compiler clause asks for no check of its own: the record is the only place that names the compiler build, and ST-GEN-UC02-R02 is changed to name the registry reference only. Option (b): the input manifest also holds the compiler build (and the registry content digest), ST-GEN-INV02 and the record format of ST-GEN-UC01-R04 are changed, and a record whose two compiler builds differ is broken. Option (c): the record's compiler build is checked against the compiler that runs drift; this makes every service broken after a compiler upgrade, so it is listed only to rule it out. Recommendation: (a), because a second copy of the compiler build in the same file adds no evidence. ST-GEN-UC02-R02-T02 waits on the answer.

title: Where is the reason for an opt-out of a default concern recorded: in the registry or with the service?
description: ST-SUP-INV15 says that the registry MUST record the reason when a declaration opts out of a default concern. ST-SUP-UC10-R02 says that STEGO MUST record the reason with the service. ST-SUP-A1-SR01 says that a run MUST NOT write to the registry sources. Reading (a): the reason is kept with the service (in its declaration and its generation record), and INV15's "the registry" means STEGO. Reading (b): the registry keeps a list of opt-outs, which a run then writes, against ST-SUP-A1-SR01. The tests ST-SUP-INV15-T and ST-SUP-UC10-R02-T01 do not assert the registry clause. Recommendation: (a), and change ST-SUP-INV15 to say that the reason is recorded with the service.

title: Does STEGO refuse a ga component that is below the quality bar, or only report it?
description: ST-SUP-INV07 says that a component MUST be ga only while it holds the quality bar at its current digest. ST-SUP-QRY05 and the step ST-SUP-UC05-FL-S04 show the quality standing of each ga component, so that a component that no longer meets the bar is seen at once; this means that a ga component below the bar can exist in the registry. Reading (a): loading or composing the registry refuses a ga component that is below the bar, so no service builds from it until the evidence is recorded again. Reading (b): the component stays ga and loads, and the quality standing (stego registry quality) reports it and exits non-zero. The test ST-SUP-INV07-T asserts only the report and the refused release, which both readings share. Recommendation: (b), because a new digest of a ga component is made by a release, and ST-SUP-INV07 already refuses that release as ga without the bar; a change to evidence alone then only needs the report.

title: Which tests are a port's correctness tests, which its conformance suite must include?
description: ST-SUP-INV18 says that a port's conformance suite MUST include the port's correctness tests. No record names the correctness tests of a port: the port (ST-SUP-EN06) has a meaning, its field meanings and the path of its conformance suite, and nothing else. As written, the first clause cannot fail. Reading (a): a port lists its correctness tests by name (a new field of the port), and the registry refuses a port whose suite lacks one of them. Reading (b): each field meaning of the port is one correctness test, and the suite must hold one test for each field, named by the field. The test ST-SUP-INV18-T proves only the second clause, the new-enemy test of authz-decision. Recommendation: (a), because a correctness property such as new-enemy is about the port as a whole, not about one field.
